paper.title: Harnessing Pre-Resolution Signals for Future Prediction Agents
paper.central_claim: Revisiting the same unresolved question yields pre-resolution signals (temporal contrasts across checkpoint notes) that, written as bounded typed patches into a persistent question-local F/E/U harness, improve later forecasts before resolution beyond repeated prediction alone; scope limited to within-question adaptation, with post-resolution check and cross-question transfer not quantified.

signatures.object: question-local typed harness H=(F,E,U) of (axis,when,guidance) procedural entries; baseline: BaseAgent under fixed prior B with no persistent state

signatures.operation: editor LLM contrasts n_t with earlier notes -> signal I_t (prediction divergence + diagnostic findings) -> patch Delta_t (add/revise/deprecate/null) -> deterministic Apply
signatures.output: H_{t+1} presented as a structured guidance block at the next checkpoint
signatures.conditions: t>=2; <=1 patch/ckpt, <=2 adds, <=5 active entries/axis; duplicates and bad references degrade to no-ops; apply order deprecate->revise->add

gap.checked_gap: Supported as a real limitation of outcome-RL/Future-as-Label style learners per the paper's own related work; residual bottleneck is within-question adaptation before resolution. Closest-neighbour texts (ACE, Reflexion, Agent KB, MemEvolve) are not in the pinned package, so the check relies on the authors' characterisation.
gap.lineage: Reflexion/ExpeL/Voyager/GEPA (editable text state) -> ACE/Agent KB/MemEvolve (evolving context/memory from execution feedback) -> Meta-Harness/AutoHarness (harness as optimisation target); forecasting side: ForecastQA/FutureX/FutureWorld benchmarks -> Halawi, outcome-RL, Future-as-Label (post-resolution supervision)
gap.closest_adjacent: ACE and Agent KB/MemEvolve (post-feedback context/memory), Reflexion (verbal reflection across trials); they use outcome or execution feedback; none uses revisit contrast with delayed ground truth per the authors
gap.residue: whether the contrast-derived signal beats generic reflection across revisits; cross-question retention; reliability of early lessons
gap.stakes: forecast quality on open questions where labels arrive late
gap.method_response: typed bounded harness writeback from note-history contrasts
gap.remaining_gap: no contrast-vs-single-note ablation, no cross-question or post-resolution evaluation, small-sample evidence
unresolved: neighbour full texts absent; test-time reflection without labels (Reflexion/Self-Refine style) not compared

It is a process-level adaptation signal derived from the agent's own repeated forecasts while ground truth (the outcome) is unavailable, which is the definition of self_supervised_signal_engineering (son55). The signal reaches the frozen predictor as a conditioning block, so adapt_via_conditioning (sol) is kept as the delivery channel. No sub-card fits: C07/C08/C26 involve training or generated data, and C03 needs a canonical schema plus an upstream phase.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In four small matched FutureWorld cells (two dates, n=28–35, three cells sharing the 05-06 questions), typed bounded writeback ends above no-persistence at T-1d by +5.5 to +8.3 points and above free-form memory in the two GPT-5.4 cells. These are single runs whose same-day noise reaches ~20 points, so the direction holds in 4/4 cells but the magnitude is uncertain. End-to-end benchmark leads are under an unequal protocol (three revisits vs single runs).
assessment.author_claim_vs_supported: Author claim (gains stem from pre-resolution-signal-driven harness evolution rather than repeated prediction alone) is supported in direction within-question; contrast-signal specificity, cross-question retention, outcome check and statistical reliability are not.
unresolved: Opus: the Δ-on-Δ headline includes T-4d offsets at an identical-by-construction checkpoint. Endpoint FH–NH gaps are +5.5 to +8.3 (opus:O01).

Opus: the '±5% compute' statement fails for the Qwen3.5 and GLM cells (opus:O08, opus:O09).
assessment.note: retained is scoped to within-question later checkpoints (not independent held-out tasks); no improver-level evidence.
assessment.evidence_level_note: Opus sides with sol. The retained typed harness is read at later checkpoints, with a same-schedule store-off arm (NH), but those checkpoints revisit the same question that produced the entries. Cross-question reuse is explicitly not quantified (App A.4/A.5, §5). EVIDENCE.md requires gains on later tasks for retained, and run precedent (r08a EvoTest, cal-dev Reflexion, r15b SpaceMind) caps same-instance reuse at task. Unlike those cases no outcome label is used before resolution, which is credited in E.holdout, not in the level.

G.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. The gap is specific: outcome-only, delayed supervision gives no process credit before resolution. The changed object (a question-local typed procedural state) is named, and Reflexion/ExpeL/ACE/Agent KB/MemEvolve/Meta-Harness are positioned. Not 4: the paper does not argue why generic multi-round reflection across revisits, which also needs no outcome, is insufficient.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. note contrast → diagnosis → bounded typed patch → deterministic apply → next-checkpoint conditioning is reconstructable. It yields distinguishable predictions: delayed separation, typed beats blob, procedure not answer. The load-bearing assumption (a note diff exposes a procedural lesson rather than mere new evidence) is plausible but untested.

X.reason: Opus sides with son55. The state boundary (only H persists), the add/revise/deprecate/null vocabulary, ≤1 patch per checkpoint, ≤2 adds, a 5-entry per-axis cap, duplicate filtering, fixed apply order and the per-checkpoint versions are all specified. Table 11 audits the realized patch stream. Not 4: there is no utility gate or rollback before resolution, the post-resolution check is unimplemented in the evaluation, and the App D prompt boxes are empty in the pinned HTML (a rendering gap, not scored as absent). sol's timing contradiction (opus:O05) concerns the validity of the pre-writeback control and is scored once, in E.causality (A2).

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. The official FutureX scorer is used and the FutureWorld scorer is fully specified, on live questions whose outcomes are unknown at prediction time. Exclusions are disclosed: resolved-only scoring, numeric items without the 8-point history dropped, 28/50 scored. The timing of the FutureWorld baseline runs is not stated.

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with sol. The design is good: NH (store-off) and GH (matched-budget generic memory) on the same schedule, a same-day repeat, and an artifact audit. Three things keep it at 2. (1) The headline Δ-on-Δ subtracts FH starts that are lower by 1–5.6 points at the identical-by-construction T-4d checkpoint. Endpoint gaps are +5.5 to +8.3 (opus:O01). (2) The 'built-in pre-writeback control' is contradicted by the flagship case, which has a harness active at T-3d (opus:O04–O06). (3) GH exists only in the two GPT-5.4 cells, and there is no note-contrast-free reflection arm. Table 1 compares three revisits against single runs. Noise magnitude is scored in E.statistics, not here (A2).

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Under the forward-only live protocol no outcome reaches the method before scoring, the harness is built only from earlier same-question notes, and the self-evolving baselines are warmed on preceding resolved data and then frozen. This fits the scoped within-question claim. The cohorts are two dates selected for ladder eligibility, and the milkyway_v5 tuning history is not stated.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder). Sample sizes, scored/launched counts and flat or negative arms are reported. No intervals, seeds or tests, and single-run swings of 16–22 points at n=28 (opus:O03, opus:O07) are comparable to the claimed gaps.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Per-question tool calls, prompt tokens and LLM calls are given at T-1d for every cell. The 'within ±5%' summary is wrong for Qwen3.5 and GLM (opus:O08, opus:O09). Editor calls, cumulative cost across checkpoints, and Milkyway's three revisits against single-run baselines in Table 1 are unaccounted.
